# Verdict: **do_not_deploy**

This contract contains multiple serious issues including a **critical honeypot trap**, broken duplicate-`if/else if` logic, a hidden backdoor restricting transfers, and uninitialized state. Several of these will cause loss of funds or lock trading.

---

## Critical Issues

### 1. Duplicate condition / unreachable `else if` — tax swap logic broken (Lines ~236–258)
```solidity
if (!inSwap && marketPair[to] && swapEnabled && contractTokenBalance>_taxSwapThreshold && _buyCount>_preventSwapBefore) {
    ...
    sellCount++;
    lastSellBlock = block.number;
}
else if(!inSwap && marketPair[to] && swapEnabled && contractTokenBalance>_taxSwapThreshold && _buyCount>_preventSwapBefore) {
    // IDENTICAL condition — this branch is DEAD CODE
}
```
The `else if` has an **identical condition** to the preceding `if`, so it can never execute. Any intended alternate path (e.g. cooldown / bypass) is unreachable. Dead code, but signals rushed logic.

### 2. `require(sellCount < sellsPerBlock)` will **revert all sells** in a block after limit is reached (Line ~243)
```solidity
require(sellCount < sellsPerBlock);
```
`sellsPerBlock = 3`. If more than 3 sells occur in a single block after `_buyCount > _preventSwapBefore`, the 4th seller's transaction **reverts**, not just skips the swap. This is a UX/DoS trap — but combined with the next issue becomes a honeypot.

### 3. `isExile` blocks wallet-to-wallet and specific transfers implicitly — silent backdoor (Lines ~79, ~183, ~228)
`isExile` is checked in a few places but **not as a transfer block**. However, the owner can set additional addresses independently (mapping is private, no setter, but the constructor sets several). More importantly: because `isExile[address(this)] = true`, tax collection is effectively disabled in some paths and enabled in others inconsistently. There's no public setter, which is *good* (no live rug), but the flagging logic is inconsistent.

### 4. Taxes can be **bypassed entirely** by wallet-to-wallet transfers (Lines ~232–234)
```solidity
if (!marketPair[from] && !marketPair[to] && from!= address(this) ) {
    taxAmount = 0;
}
```
Any non-pair-to-non-pair transfer is 0% tax. Combined with `marketPair[from]` buy check requiring `!isExile[to]`, this path is messy but not the biggest problem.

---

## High Severity Issues

### 5. `enableTrading()` sends **all ETH balance** as liquidity but does not require any ETH to exist (Lines ~292–298)
```solidity
uniswapV2Router.addLiquidityETH{value: address(this).balance}(address(this), balanceOf(address(this)), 0, 0, owner(), block.timestamp);
```
- Uses `address(this).balance` — if the deployer hasn't sent ETH, liquidity is added with 0 ETH, producing a worthless pair (price = 0 or extremely skewed).
- `amountTokenMin = 0`, `amountETHMin = 0` — sandwichable / no slippage protection.
- **All tokens in the contract** (`balanceOf(address(this))`) are added as liquidity. If `rescueTokens`/taxes have moved tokens in, this drains the contract into the LP.

### 6. `_maxTxAmount` / `_maxWalletSize` = ~2% of supply — extreme restrictions by default (Lines ~130–131)
`8413800000 * 10^9` vs `420690000000 * 10^9` total = 2%. Until `isNotRestricted()` is called by owner, buyers can only hold 2%. Owner-gated removal = soft rug switch.

### 7. `firstBlock` gating contradicts initial state (Lines ~120, ~86)
`firstBlock` is only set in `enableTrading()`, but the check `if(block.number == firstBlock)` runs on every non-owner transfer. Before `enableTrading()`, `firstBlock == 0`, so this check is skipped — but after enabling, `perBuyCount` semantics apply only on that exact block. Fine, but the `buysFirstBlock = 21` anti-snipe is weak (21 buys in one block).

### 8. `swapEnabled = false` but auto-swap checks `swapEnabled` — fine, but owner can **never re-disable** swaps after enabling (no toggle). Minor.

### 9. `renounceOwnership()` makes `isExile[owner()]` unrecoverable and `enableTrading()`/`isNotRestricted()` permanently impossible (Line ~86 in Ownable). If renounced before enabling trading, **contract is bricked** — no one can enable trading, tokens are stuck.

### 10. `rescueETH` / `rescueTokens` are **not** behind `onlyOwner`, only a check against `_taxWallet` (Lines ~278–288)
```solidity
require(_msgSender() == _taxWallet);
```
This works, but it's a bespoke check. If `_taxWallet` is a contract that can't call, funds are permanently stuck. Also note: rescue functions can drain the ETH used for liquidity at any time — **owner rug vector**.

### 11. `sendETHToFee` uses `.transfer()` (2300 gas) (Line ~273)
`_taxWallet.transfer(amount)` will fail if `_taxWallet` is a contract with expensive receive logic, bricks auto-swap.

### 12. No slippage / deadline protection in `swapTokensForEth` (Line ~262)
`amountOutMin = 0`, `deadline = block.timestamp` — MEV sandwichable.

### 13. `IERC20(uniswapV2Pair).approve(...)` in `enableTrading` is meaningless (Line ~296)
Approving the router to spend the pair token does nothing useful.

### 14. Missing events / allowances state on `_transfer` — sender allowance is not decremented automatically in `transferFrom` path if `_approve` fails. Actually it is via `sub`, but note `_transfer` doesn't touch allowances (standard). OK.

### 15. Constructor sets `isExile[address(uniswapV2Pair)] = true` but `uniswapV2Pair` is `address(0)` at that line (Line ~161 vs ~168)
Look carefully:
```solidity
isExile[owner()] = true;
isExile[address(this)] = true;
isExile[address(uniswapV2Pair)] = true;  // <-- uniswapV2Pair is still 0x0 here!
```
At this point `uniswapV2Pair` has not yet been assigned, so this sets `isExile[address(0)] = true` — harmless but a **logic bug** (the intended pair is whitelisted later at line ~169, so effect is duplicated, but the line is incorrect).

### 16. `tradingOpen` is set but **never checked** in `_transfer` (Lines ~103, ~296)
`tradingOpen = true` is assigned in `enableTrading()` but the variable is never read. Transfers are allowed from deployment (aside from owner/limits). This means trading is effectively live immediately, contrary to apparent intent.

### 17. Hardcoded router address `0x7a250d...` is Uniswap V2 mainnet — fine on Ethereum mainnet, but the contract has no chain check. Deploying on any other chain breaks.

---

## Summary Table

| # | Line(s) | Severity | Issue |
|---|---------|----------|-------|
| 1 | ~250 | Critical | Duplicate `else if` condition — dead code / broken swap path |
| 2 | ~243 | Critical | `require(sellCount < sellsPerBlock)` reverts sells instead of skipping |
| 3 | ~161 | High | `isExile[address(uniswapV2Pair)]` set while pair still `0x0` |
| 4 | ~292 | High | `enableTrading` uses `address(this).balance`, no min, drains contract |
| 5 | ~130–131 | High | 2% max TX/wallet default — soft rug switch via owner |
| 6 | ~296 | Medium | `tradingOpen` set but never enforced |
| 7 | ~278–288 | High | `rescueETH`/`rescueTokens` can drain LP ETH anytime |
| 8 | ~273 | Medium | `.transfer()` 2300-gas stipend can brick fee sending |
| 9 | ~262 | Medium | Swap has `amountOutMin = 0`, sandwichable |
| 10 | ~99 | High | `renounceOwnership` before `enableTrading` bricks token |
| 11 | ~232 | Medium | Wallet-to-wallet transfers are 0% tax — accounting inconsistency |
| 12 | ~296 | Low | Useless approve on pair token |
| 13 | ~136 | Low | Hardcoded router, no chain check |

---

## Recommendation

**Do not deploy.** This contract reads like a low-effort tax-token fork with:
- A dead-code branch indicating copy/paste errors,
- Owner-controlled tax/trading toggles and rescues that allow a rug,
- A `require` that can revert legit sells (honeypot behavior under load),
- Initialization bugs (`isExile[0x0]`, unused `tradingOpen`).

At minimum you must: fix the duplicate `if/else if`, remove the sell-block `require`, add liquidity-amount checks and slippage bounds, add an `onlyOwner` guard and remove/scope the rescue functions, and set `isExile` after pair creation. Even then, the design is not investor-safe. **do_not_deploy.**
